analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-poison occurs because Compiler::simplifyExpression caches references to BinaryExpression children (`Expression& left = *bin->left(); Expression& right = *bin->right();`), then performs rewrite helpers like `delete_left`, `delete_right`, `vectorize_left/right` that can replace/move/destroy those child expressions, but the function continues to use the stale `leftType/rightType` (and potentially `left/right`) afterward. This leaves dangling Type/Expression references and eventually reads poisoned memory in `Type::isScalar()` during optimization. Crash is observed in `Type::isScalar` (SkSLType.h:352), but root cause is invalid lifetime handling in `simplifyExpression`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via `SkRuntimeEffect::Make` on crafted SkSL that drives optimizer rewrites in `scanCFG`/`simplifyExpression` for binary expressions (e.g., expressions like `an(), float[](), float[]()` in the PoC). During optimization (`convertProgram` -> `optimize` -> `scanCFG`), binary simplification performs a transformation that mutates/replaces one operand, then later logic still consults previously-captured operand/type references, causing a read from freed/poisoned pool memory.
